transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Over the last month I’ve just lost interest in my art, dancing, and even my job, and I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to. It just feels like all the things that used to bring me joy have gone completely flat.
Have you experienced similar periods of low mood and loss of interest in the past, or is this the first time you have ever felt this way?

Looking back, these swings between feeling overly energized and then sinking into these heavy, low moods have been happening off and on for about five months now. It all really started around the time the busy tax season began at my work.
During those times when you felt overly energized, did you notice a decreased need for sleep, or did you find yourself talking much faster or taking on many more projects than usual?

Yes, definitely. I was only sleeping three or four hours a night but felt completely wired, and my coworkers even teased me for talking a mile a minute like I'd had too much coffee. I also took on a massive amount of extra projects, staying late to redo spreadsheets at work while trying to launch a side business and attend every social event possible.
During those high-energy periods, did those symptoms last for at least four consecutive days, and were they noticeable enough to cause a clear change in your functioning at work or with others?

Yes, that high-energy phase lasted for a few weeks straight during the busy tax season, so it was definitely longer than four days. It was very noticeable to everyone around me, especially my coworkers who joked that I was on a caffeine high because I was talking a mile a minute and taking on everyone's extra spreadsheets. I was staying up late working on all kinds of projects without ever feeling tired, which was a huge, obvious change from my normal self.
During those high-energy periods, did you ever feel like you were losing touch with reality, such as believing you had special powers or hearing things that others could not hear?

No, I never experienced anything like hearing voices or losing touch with reality, and I didn't think I had supernatural powers. Even though my thoughts were racing and I felt incredibly confident—like I was fully capable of running my own business right then—I always knew what was real.

During these periods when you feel low and lose interest, do you find that you are still able to function at work and in your daily life, or do your symptoms make it impossible to carry out your normal responsibilities?

Honestly, it's been really hard to keep up with anything, and I feel so embarrassed about it. I've been pulled into meetings at work because I'm making mistakes in the ledgers, and I've completely stopped going to my salsa classes and community events. At home, everything is piling up—I'm living out of laundry baskets and the dishes are just sitting in the sink because I'm too exhausted to care.
During these low periods, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or have you felt like you are unable to function at all in your daily life?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of ending my life, but I do feel completely unable to keep up with my daily responsibilities. I'm making mistakes at work that have led to meetings, skipping the salsa classes and community events I love, and letting chores like dishes and laundry pile up at home because I just don't have the energy.
During these low periods, have you experienced any physical symptoms like significant changes in your appetite or weight, or do you find yourself moving or speaking much more slowly than usual?

Yes, I've completely lost my appetite and have to force myself to eat even half a sandwich, and I've noticed my pants are getting loose. I also feel like I'm moving underwater now—walking slower and staring at my screen before typing, which is the total opposite of how fast I was flying through work a few weeks ago.
During these low periods, would you say your level of functioning is so severely impaired that you have been unable to perform your job duties at all, or perhaps required hospitalization?

No, I haven't been hospitalized and I am still going to work, but my functioning is definitely impaired. I've been making mistakes that led to meetings about my accuracy, and I'm falling behind on chores at home and skipping social events. But I haven't been completely unable to work or anything like that.

During these low periods, have you felt that your symptoms are severe enough to cause significant distress or impairment in your social or occupational functioning, even if you are still managing to show up to work?

Yes, it has caused so much distress and honestly makes me feel really embarrassed. At work, I've been pulled into meetings because of accuracy errors I never used to make, and socially, I've stopped going to the salsa classes and community events I love. At home, I'm just so overwhelmed that dishes are piling up and I'm living out of laundry baskets because I don't have the energy to keep up.

The depressive episode involves significant impairment in functioning (work errors, social withdrawal, neglect of chores) and physical symptoms (appetite loss/weight loss, psychomotor retardation), but lacks psychotic features and has not required hospitalization. Given that the current episode is depressive and the patient is experiencing significant distress and impairment without the severity of a manic episode or psychotic features, F31.3 (Bipolar disorder, current episode mild or moderate depression) is the most accurate fit.
